summary: A proposal for two changes to the IMP-Host protocol defined in BBN Report 1822. The first covers the 30-second timeout when the IMP sends to a Host, declaring an unresponsive Host dead to the network. The second proposes a new timeout for the Host-to-IMP direction. Comments were invited, with installation planned for October 10 absent objections.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC proposes two timeout changes for communication between an IMP and a Host. One would identify an unresponsive Host as dead to the network; the other would notify a Host when the IMP cannot process its message promptly.

subtitle: Two proposed timeout changes to the IMP-Host protocol.

tldr.problem: An unresponsive Host could make other hosts wait, while an IMP waiting for internal resources could stall a Host's transmission without notice.
tldr.mechanism: The proposals would declare a nonresponsive Host dead until it sends again and send a type 9, subtype 4 message if the IMP cannot process a message within 15 seconds.
tldr.outcome: The two changes are independent and were open to comment before planned installation. The unit metadata says RFC 394 updates RFC 381.

sections.title: Two Independent Proposals
sections.content:
The RFC describes two proposed changes to the IMP-Host protocol in BBN Report 1822, as revised in RFC 381. One concerns the IMP-to-Host interface and its existing 30-second timeout; the other concerns Host-to-IMP messages.

The changes are independent in statement and implementation. The authors invite comments and state an intended installation date if no adverse comments arrive.
sections.plainLanguage: BBN proposes two separate changes to IMP-Host timing. The RFC invites comments before installation.

sections.title: Declaring an Unresponsive Host Dead
sections.content:
Under the described procedure, a Host has 30 seconds to accept each packet of regular or non-regular messages. If it does not respond, the IMP discards messages held for it, notifies the source Hosts, cycles its Ready Line, sends NOPs and sends an interface-reset message.

The proposal adds that the IMP declare the Host dead to the network. When the IMP next receives a bit from that Host, it declares the Host alive and begins a 30-second delay while that information propagates.
sections.plainLanguage: If a Host fails to respond, the IMP would mark it dead so other hosts can learn that it is unavailable. The Host becomes alive again when it sends a bit to the IMP.

sections.title: A Host-to-IMP Resource Timeout
sections.content:
An IMP needs internal resources, such as a message number and table entry, to process a Host message. If these resources are unavailable, the interface can stop while the IMP waits. The RFC notes that this can be especially difficult for half-duplex Hosts.

The proposal has the IMP try for 15 seconds, then send a type 9, subtype 4 message meaning Incomplete Transmission - Resources Unavailable. No part of the message has entered the network; after the remainder is taken in, the Host may retransmit if desired.
sections.plainLanguage: If the IMP cannot process a message because resources are unavailable, it would notify the Host after 15 seconds. The Host could then choose to send the message again.

references.text: RFC 381, the revision to BBN Report 1822 that RFC 394 updates.
